about: The GEN worker's step shell of the Kimi K3 SM107 Helix16 ULL target (runtime.py), re-sourced from the served tree user/xguan/k3-rubin-ull-chain-mlamoe-gsm @ 6904cd9672 (measured as 1007804), whose target declared ull_step_shell = StepShell(step_prep=True, step_fold=True, pin_executor=True, gil_switch_us=200). Each entry: our name -> served path:function @ 6904cd9672, or the HEAD (#21996) code we reuse. The served kernel files are byte copies listed in kernels/SOURCE.json (kernels/step/).

staged_uploads.about: Served staged these uploads into the commit (input_commit.stage). Ours reach the pack through #21996's step_inputs.copy_ (already routed in HEAD) or step_inputs.copy_metadata_ (routed here; a plain copy unless the open pack sets issue_after_prepare).
staged_uploads.prompt_lens_cuda: copy_metadata_ through h2d_cache.copy_h2d_pool_shared(pack=True) without an H2D skip cache

deliberate_differences: The pack opens on every replay of an already captured decode graph (#21996's pack condition). Served opened its commit only on a generation-only graph step without padding dummies on a one-model linear speculative engine; on this deployment (graphs 1..4, batch <= 4, DSpark one-model) both cover every steady step.

The commit's overlap fixup reads the previous step's sequence slots from the engine's device buffer (previous_batch_indices_cuda, uploaded by #21996 only when the slots change) instead of staging them into the arena each step (kernels/step/input_commit.py local edit slots_device).

Executor pinning and the GIL interval run in ExecutorEvents.before_overlap_loop, on the executor thread right before the loop's profiler and hang-detector scope; served ran them right inside that scope. Same thread, before the first iteration.

StepFold has no A/B period, no suppress switch and no execution-stream registration: served used the stream only for the mamba state-index upload fold, which needs TRTLLM_STATE_INDEX_COPY_KERNEL (=1 in 1007804 (1007804's GEN srun --export; the case's trtllm_config.yaml lacks it); it writes only when the indices change, so a steady decode batch never folds it).

Not ported: the DFlash draft-history snapshot kernel (served step_fold, k3_rubin/spec/history_snapshot.py). #21996's target decodes the draft table on the device and publishes no draft history; owned by the draft-cache area.

fold_block_offsets_copy is provided, but its caller (the KV cache manager's copy_batch_block_offsets, cache.py) belongs to the KV area and is not wired yet; until it is, the block-offset copy stays #21996's copyBatchBlockOffsetsToDevice launch between the replays.
physical_gpu_index reads CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES as served does (device topology, not a switch).

With spec_step_fold set, #21996's one-model sampler stores its outputs through _scatter_to_stores (4 index_copy_), which is served's path; without it, SM100/SM103 (GB300) would take #21996's one-launch SlotScatter, and SM107 (Rubin) the same 4 index_copy_ (spec_step_copies.is_supported excludes SM107).
